title: Ethiopian Christmas Sweet (Genna)
community: Ethiopian Orthodox Christians — the Christmas (January 7th) sweet
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Christmas Cookies — spiced honey cookies made specifically for Genna (Ethiopian Christmas, January 7th) after the 43-day Advent fast. Shaped as stars and crosses using the symbolism of the Ethiopian Orthodox tradition, they are the first sweets eaten after Advent.
longDesc: Genna cookies are the first sweet after 43 days of fasting — the breaking of Advent fast with honey cookies in Christmas shapes (stars, crosses) is a moment of pure joy. The Ethiopian Christmas sweet.
ingredients: // Same as ETH191 (Honey Cookies) — use the full recipe
// But shape as stars and crosses for Genna
// And add: ¼ tsp ground black pepper (Ethiopian Christmas spice touch)
steps: Make honey cookie dough as per ETH191.
Add black pepper to the spice blend.
Roll and cut into star and cross shapes.
Bake and cool as per ETH191.
Optional: decorate with honey glaze drizzle in cross patterns.
chefTips: The cross shape is the Ethiopian Orthodox Christian symbol.
Black pepper is the additional Genna spice.
culturalNote: Genna cookies are the taste of Ethiopian Christmas morning — after the overnight church service, after the Christmas dawn celebration, the first sweet thing eaten after 43 days of fasting. A star-shaped honey cookie from a grandmother is one of the most emotionally significant foods in Ethiopian Orthodox life.
